approach: Add `check_defined_terms(reading, request)` to crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs as one `step!` in `refusing_check`, right after `check_environment_reach` and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`. It reduces the request to plain prose, finds the whole words ladder, rung, tier and layer (plus plural and possessive forms), and refuses a reading that has a capability and no question when a used term has no `Term <word>:` assumption. Plain prose means the request without three things. First, the generated root-cause lines: an `Introspection <id> (job <job>); prevention it proposed:` line is skipped by its exact shape, and the `Cause:`, `Failure class:` and `Fix the root cause of a repeated failure:` lines are skipped only when the request also holds hestia's own opening sentence. Second, quoted spans. Third, parenthesised example lists (two or more commas, or an example opener). Code-like tokens are also dropped. The rule is also written as an eighth `READING_RULES` line in briefs.rs, which is not the budgeted reader prompt. The change adds corpus cases and input forms, updates the cited-jobs replay (g6vy by `check_outcome_state`, 7bf8 by `check_defined_terms`, 0wtc by none), rewrites one `check_outcome_state` doc sentence, and adds a CHANGELOG entry and D164. The doc comment, CHANGELOG and D164 declare `expected 3% of newly refused readings`, an estimate. They state that the measured share is recorded by the loop replay at verification, and that the producer cannot see it unless a held send-back reports it. They also state the known false refusals: priority tiers, caching layers, and the repo's own ladder and rung.

decisions.choice: Match structural words in plain request prose only: a `plain_request_prose` pre-pass, then the existing `request_words` tokenizer, then whole-word comparison (term, term+s, with a trailing `'s` stripped from the token first).
decisions.reason: `request_words` (reading.rs:3507) splits all text and ignores quoting, and its tokens keep `'` between letters, so "ladder's" would match nothing. The 7bf8 request quotes 'a ladder of requirements' and also uses the term in plain prose, so the pre-pass must drop the first and keep the second. Whole-word tokens keep stepladder, delayer, `ladder.md` and `layer_count` out.

rejected.option: Run `request_words` over the whole request
rejected.why: It ignores quoting, so generated root-cause requests (hestia.rs:466-489) that only quote the words would be refused.

rejected.option: Substring match
rejected.why: It refuses stepladder and delayer, which criterion 3 requires to pass.

rejected.option: Treat every parenthesised span as a non-use
rejected.why: It hides real uses such as '(the ladder, which ranks requirements)'.

decisions.choice: Skip generated lines by their exact shape. (1) An `Introspection ` line is skipped only if it also holds ` (job ` and `); prevention it proposed:`, the form at hestia.rs:486-488. (2) `Failure class: `, `Cause: ` and `Fix the root cause of a repeated failure: ` lines are skipped only in that exact case and only when the request holds hestia's opening sentence 'The same cause has produced failures in more than one job.' (hestia.rs:467).
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3. The bare prefixes would drop a hand-written line such as 'Introspection of the ladder is needed.' or 'Cause: the ladder has no rung' whole, hiding real uses. The anchor sentence and the full line shape tie the skip to text Athena generated. A unit case pins that 'Introspection of the ladder is needed.' and a hand-written 'Cause: the ladder is undefined' (no anchor) are still uses.

rejected.option: Skip any line that starts with introspection, cause: or failure class: (the previous plan)
rejected.why: Case-insensitive bare prefixes drop hand-written lines that use a term.

rejected.option: Do not skip generated lines and rely on quote stripping
rejected.why: The generated Cause and prevention text is free prose from earlier introspections, so it is not quoted.

decisions.choice: Quote and parenthesis handling: remove straight and curly double-quoted spans, backtick pairs, and single-quoted spans (opener after start/whitespace/`(` and before a letter or digit; closer after a non-space and before a non-alphanumeric; an unclosed opener stays as text). Scan per line. Remove a parenthesised span only if it has two or more commas or opens with e.g., i.e., such as, for example or like. Replace whitespace-delimited tokens containing `/`, `_` or `::` with a space.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4. A single-comma parenthetical such as '(the ladder, which ranks requirements)' is a real use and stays counted. A list like '(ladder, layer, tier)' has two commas and is dropped. Per-line scanning means a stray apostrophe cannot swallow the rest of the request.

rejected.option: Drop any parenthesised span that holds a comma (the previous plan)
rejected.why: It hides a real use with a single comma.

decisions.choice: A term is defined by an assumption that, trimmed and lowercased, starts `term <word>:` followed by at least 3 words. The word is normalised by dropping a trailing `s` or `'s` when the base form is in STRUCTURAL_TERMS, so `Term layers:` defines layer. The line may cite the defining file. No criterion naming the term is required.
decisions.reason: This copies the `Code survey:` convention (`code_surveys`, reading.rs:3832), which the reader already knows. It needs no new reading field. The normalisation (finding 4) stops a plural definition from being refused as undefined.

rejected.option: Read docs/ontology.toml
rejected.why: Out of scope in the brief.

rejected.option: Also require a behavior criterion that names the term
rejected.why: A second condition for little gain. Criterion 1's accepted case carries one anyway.

rejected.option: Accept a definition in the reading summary
rejected.why: The summary has no fixed label, so a check on it would be lexical guessing.

decisions.choice: Place the step after `check_environment_reach` (reading.rs:3252) and before `check_boundary_and_repo_files`.
decisions.reason: Existing tests pin governance then outcome_state, and outcome_state then environment_reach (reading.rs:8850 region). The new check reads only the reading and request, so it belongs before the file-comparing checks. `an_extra_check_with_no_case_is_reported` anchors on `check_reading_references`, which is unaffected.

rejected.option: Right after check_outcome_state
rejected.why: It breaks the environment_reach adjacency test.

rejected.option: Last
rejected.why: A missing file would be reported first, and the cheaper request-and-reading check would run last.

decisions.choice: Keep the four-word list (fixed by the brief) and state the false-refusal class as intended: plain technical uses of 'tier' (Athena's priority tiers: plan.rs, drain.rs, config.rs, display.rs) and 'layer' (a caching layer), and the repo's own ladder and rung, are refused until a `Term` line restates them. Pin the class with a corpus case that expects a refusal.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2. Narrowing the list is a user decision the brief has already made. Stating the limit in the doc comment and D164, and pinning it with a refusing case, makes any later narrowing a visible test change.

rejected.option: Drop 'tier' and 'layer' to cut false refusals
rejected.why: The brief fixes the list.

rejected.option: Leave the false-refusal class unstated
rejected.why: The refusal rate would be understated to the reader and the verifier.

decisions.choice: State the measurement path honestly. The doc comment, CHANGELOG and D164 declare 'expected 3% of newly refused readings' as an estimate. They say the measured share is recorded in the job's replay record at verification (`replay_stage` then `run.record`), where the verifier sees it, and is shown to the producer only in a held send-back (`replay_problem`, which reports the percent and the limit). The producer writes a measured figure only if a send-back reports one. No test asserts a measured figure.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. run/producer.rs:370-399 passes the replay to the producer only as a held problem. The producer snapshot has no records/, so it cannot run the replay. A needle for a measured share could never be satisfied reliably.

rejected.option: Producer reads the loop-replay line and writes the measured value (the previous plan)
rejected.why: The line goes to Athena's UI, which the producer cannot read.

rejected.option: A test needle for 'measured share where it differs'
rejected.why: The producer cannot know whether the share differs, so the needle is unsatisfiable.

risks.risk: The 3% figure is an estimate. The planner cannot see records/, the producer cannot run the loop replay, and the real share of past requests that use these words in plain prose is unknown. Tier and layer are common words.
risks.mitigation: The text labels 3% an estimate and says the measured share is recorded in the replay record at verification, where the verifier sees it. The producer writes a measured figure only if a held send-back (`replay_problem`) reports one. Over 8%, the producer narrows false refusals (for example the code-token skip) and reports the rest. The tier and layer question is open to the user.

risks.risk: Quote handling over-strips (a stray apostrophe swallows a use) or under-strips (a quoted mention is counted).
risks.mitigation: Scan per line and leave an unclosed opener as text. Unit tests cover apostrophes in "Sri's" and "don't", an unclosed quote, curly quotes, backticks, possessive "ladder's" (counted as a use), and a plain use beside quotes (companion corpus case, refused).

risks.risk: The generated-line skip drops a hand-written line, or fails to skip a generated one.
risks.mitigation: Skip by exact shape. An Introspection line needs ' (job ' and '); prevention it proposed:'. Cause:, Failure class: and the title line need hestia's opening sentence. Unit cases pin both directions. If hestia.rs changes its wording, the corpus case built on `root_cause_request` fails, which is visible.

risks.risk: A parenthesised list with a single comma, such as '(ladder, layer)', is counted as a use, and a long parenthetical with two commas that holds a real use is dropped.
risks.mitigation: The rule (two or more commas, or an example opener) is stated in the doc comment and covered by unit cases for each shape. The residual error is a false refusal, which the reader repairs with a Term line, and not a silent acceptance of a main use.

risks.risk: The rules section in briefs.rs exceeds the 2600-byte bound with an eighth line. I estimated about 2570 bytes, which is not a measurement.
risks.mitigation: Run `cargo test -p athena-context`. The failure prints the actual section length, and the producer sets the bound just above it. The new line stays at or under 220 characters.

risks.risk: 0wtc could be wrongly claimed as caught or not caught, because the real recorded request may differ from the text in CITED_REQUESTS.
risks.mitigation: The 0wtc assertion is `outcome.is_none()` on the text at refusal_controls refusal_corpus.rs:467-472, which holds no structural word. The doc comment and D164 state that the Hermes term is not covered.

risks.risk: A new corpus case is refused first by an earlier check (an unknown path, a bullet count mismatch), so it fails for the wrong reason.

dependents.name: Words tier, ladder, rung and layer in other modules
dependents.dependent: crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs (lines about 421, 497, 733-741), drain.rs (about 612), config.rs (about 59), display.rs (about 584), steward.rs and crates/athena-cli/tests, which use 'tier', 'ladder' and 'rung' as Rust identifiers, plan fields and priority-tier wording

demonstrations.method: Run the real gate `refusing_check` on two corpus cases built from the recorded 7bf8 request (shared const `REQUEST_7BF8`, extracted from `CITED_REQUESTS`, refusal_corpus.rs:456). Case A, `structural-term-ladder-undefined-in-7bf8-request`, uses `base_reading` with no Term line and is expected to be refused by check_defined_terms. Case B, `structural-term-ladder-defined-and-named-by-a-behavior-criterion-accepted`, adds an assumption `Term ladder: ...` that cites docs/guide.md (in `repo_files()`) and a behavior criterion that names the ladder via `with_behavior`. It is expected to be accepted. An added reading.rs unit test also checks that a request using 'ladder' with a reading that has `Term ladders: ...` is accepted (normalisation).
demonstrations.observes: Case A returns Some(("check_defined_terms", err)). The error starts 'the reading was refused because', names ladder and shows the `Term ladder:` repair. Case B returns None. `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` and `the_wrapper_agrees_with_refusing_check_on_every_case` pass. I read the test names and case structure and ran nothing.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without `check_defined_terms` and its step line, Case A is accepted instead of refused and `corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome` fails. If the check ignored the Term line, Case B would be refused.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `athena_core::reading::refusing_check` (exists, reading.rs:3228), reached through `check_reading_acceptance`. Fixture: the corpus `Case` struct, `base_reading` and `with_behavior`, injected through `cases()` (exist, refusal_corpus.rs). Step 4 adds the shared const and the two cases. Nothing is doubled.

demonstrations.method: Run the real gate on the case `structural-term-quoted-or-cited-mentions-are-accepted`. Its request is built with the existing `root_cause_request(&[...])` helper, so it has the real generated lines: the opening sentence, a `Failure class:` line, a `Cause:` line and `Introspection <id> (job <job>); prevention it proposed: ...` lines. The extra lines mention ladder, layer and tier only inside those generated lines, inside a double-quoted word, a single-quoted word, and a parenthesised list '(ladder, layer, tier)'. `base_reading` has no Term lines and `referenced` is set as in `root-cause-cites-two-jobs-without-relying`. `Case.source` reads 'job 20261107-110049-k8c2, rebuilt from the job brief and the line forms at hestia.rs:466-489; not the recorded request (records/ is absent)'. Companion cases: `structural-term-plain-use-beside-quoted-mentions-is-refused` (the same plus 'Use the ladder to decide what to change.', refused) and `structural-term-possessive-use-is-refused` ('the ladder's rungs', refused). Unit tests in reading.rs call `check_defined_terms` on each quoting shape and pin that a hand-written 'Introspection of the ladder is needed.' and a hand-written 'Cause: the ladder is undefined' with no anchor sentence are still uses. The form tags `structural-term-plain-prose`, `structural-term-quoted-or-cited` and `structural-term-defined` are added to INPUT_FORMS (34 becomes 37).
demonstrations.observes: The quoted-only root-cause request gives None from `refusing_check` with a reading that has no Term lines. The companion cases give Some("check_defined_terms"). `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms` passes because each new tag has a case.
demonstrations.fails_without: If quoted or generated mentions counted as uses, the accepted case is refused by check_defined_terms. If the generated-line skip were removed, `defined_terms_ignores_generated_lines_quotes_and_parentheses` fails. If the skip were a blanket one, the plain-use companion would be accepted and fail. If the bare-prefix skip came back, the hand-written Introspection and Cause unit cases would fail.
demonstrations.seam: `refusing_check` (exists). `root_cause_request` and `earlier()` in refusal_corpus.rs (exist, about lines 236 and 224). The unit tests use `governed_reading` in reading.rs tests (exists). Step 4 adds the cases and tags. The matcher is real and nothing is doubled.

demonstrations.method: Run the real gate on `structural-term-inside-other-words-is-accepted` ('Rename the stepladder helper and remove the delayer module.', tagged with the existing form `trigger-word-inside-other-word`). The unit test `defined_terms_matches_whole_words_only` also checks requests with no structural word, `ladder.md`, `layer_count`, the path `crates/x/layer/mod.rs`, and a quoted 'layer'. A check that refused requests with no structural word would fail the existing accepted corpus cases such as `steward-three-dash-bullets`.

demonstrations.method: Gate-level tests, with no extractor test. `defined_terms_refusal_needs_the_step_line` (reading.rs, same shape as `history_fixture_refusal_needs_the_step_line`, reading.rs:10552-10567) builds a reading with a capability that is missing the Term line. It asserts `refuser_for(reading, request) == Some("check_defined_terms")` and `accept(..)` is an error, and that the `refusing_check` body contains `step!(check_defined_terms(reading, request));`. `defined_terms_has_one_step_line_after_environment_reach` pins the position, in the style of `environment_reach_has_one_step_line`. The existing `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` (refusal_corpus.rs about 1429) requires a refusing corpus case for every step line, and passes through Case A of criterion 1.
demonstrations.observes: The gate refuses the undefined-ladder reading under the name `check_defined_terms`. The body holds exactly one such step line. Every step line has a refusing corpus case.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the `step!(check_defined_terms(...))` line removed, `refusing_check` returns None for the undefined-ladder reading. Then `defined_terms_refusal_needs_the_step_line`, `defined_terms_has_one_step_line_after_environment_reach` and the corpus refusing case all fail. With the line present but no refusing corpus case, `every_acceptance_check_has_a_refusing_corpus_case` fails.

demonstrations.method: Test `defined_terms_refusal_is_declared_intended` in reading.rs, in the style of `outcome_state_refusal_is_declared_intended` (about reading.rs:8413). `replay_declaration` on 'expected 3% of newly refused readings' gives share Some(3). The doc comment of `check_defined_terms`, CHANGELOG.md and D164 must each contain 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended.' and 'estimate', and must say that ladder and rung are refused until restated, and that plain uses of 'tier' (priority tiers) and 'layer' (caching layer) are refused too. They must also say the measured share is recorded in the job's replay record at verification. There is no needle for a measured figure. The `check_outcome_state` doc must contain 'check_defined_terms' and not 'which does not catch them', and keep 'covers 1 of the 3 cited jobs', the three job ids and 'outside the check'. A corpus case `structural-term-priority-tier-is-refused` ('Demote an item one tier when its tier is full.', and a second request 'add a caching layer', both refused by check_defined_terms) pins the known false refusal.
demonstrations.observes: The declared figure parses to 3. Each document carries the sentence, the estimate, and the false-refusal and recording statements. The old 'outside any check' wording is gone. The priority-tier and caching-layer requests are refused.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the doc comment, CHANGELOG or D164 omits the sentence, the limits or the recording path, the test fails. If the check_outcome_state doc still says the other two jobs are outside any check, the guard fails. If a later change narrowed 'tier' or 'layer', the pinning case fails visibly.

open_questions: User: If the replay at verification records more than 8% of newly refused readings (the declared 3% plus the 5-point margin), should the list drop 'layer' or 'tier', or should the declared share rise through a revised reading? The planner cannot see records/, and the producer can neither run the replay nor edit the accepted reading's declared figure.

User: Should hand-written requests that use 'tier' (Athena's priority tiers) or 'layer' (a caching layer) in a plain technical sense, and requests about the repo's own ladder and rung, stay refused until the reading restates them with a Term line? This plan says yes and pins it with a corpus case, as the brief fixes the list.
